title: Global, object-specific, and quick actions
objectives: Define a quick action as a reusable action users launch from Lightning and mobile action bars.
Choose a global action when the work is not tied to a specific record; choose an object-specific action when it is.
Place actions on page layouts or Lightning pages (including Dynamic Actions) separately from creating the action metadata.
Refuse an action when the need is a validation rule, a formula field, or a full custom app.
diagnostic_question: Users need a one-tap Create Inspection from a property, a Create Vendor that works from the header with no record open, and a Log a Call on the property. Which are global versus object-specific quick actions, and where do you add them so they appear?
definition: Quick actions are actions users launch from Lightning Experience and the Salesforce mobile app to create or update records, log calls, or open custom UI. Global actions are not tied to a particular object or record and are managed on the global publisher layout. Object-specific actions belong to an object and can create records automatically related to the current record. Creating an action is metadata; showing it requires adding it to a page layout's Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions or to a Lightning page (including Dynamic Actions). ([Actions Overview](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_overview.htm); [Global Actions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_global.htm); [Object-Specific Actions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_objectspecific.htm); [Page Layouts](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=customize_layout.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for global versus object-specific, and for 'I created it but it does not show' because the action was never added to a layout or Lightning page. An object-specific Create can prefill the relationship to the current record; a global Create cannot. Actions are not validation rules and not FLS.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a hotel. A global quick action is the lobby kiosk—any guest can create a wake-up request without being in a room. An object-specific quick action is the in-room phone that already knows this stay: Create Inspection from this property. The quick action is the labeled button itself. Hanging the button on the wall is the page layout or Lightning page. A security gate (validation) still stops a bad suitcase even if the button is huge.
deeper_explanation: Actions Overview Help frames quick actions as productivity shortcuts in Lightning and mobile. Types typically include create, update, log a call, and custom (Visualforce, Aura, LWC, or Flow)—confirm the current type list in the create-action wizard rather than inventing types. ([Actions Overview](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_overview.htm))

Global actions live independently of a record. They are added to the global publisher layout (and can also appear in other supported action lists). A global Create cannot automatically relate to 'this' record because there may be no this. ([Global Actions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_global.htm))

Object-specific actions are created on an object. A create action can set the new record's relationship to the current record. They appear when you add them to that object's page layout action section or to the object's Lightning record page. ([Object-Specific Actions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.actions_objectspecific.htm); [Page Layouts](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=customize_layout.htm))

Dynamic Actions on a Lightning record page can show or hide actions with visibility rules, similar in spirit to Dynamic Forms (DATA-009). Exact availability is object- and release-sensitive—Needs verification. Until then, the layout action bar is the usual assignment surface.
Action layouts choose which fields appear on the create/update form. That is not the object's page layout and not FLS. Validation rules still fire on save from an action.

mental_model.analogy: A hotel: global actions are lobby kiosks, object-specific actions are in-room phones that already know the stay, and the page layout or Lightning page is the wall you hang the button on.
useful_mapping: global action → lobby kiosk, no room context
object-specific action → in-room phone bound to this property
action layout → which fields the form asks for
page layout action bar → hanging the button on that room style
global publisher layout → hanging buttons in the lobby
validation rule → the security gate that still runs on save
where_it_breaks: Some actions open Flow or LWC, which is more than a paper button.
Dynamic Actions assignment is not a physical wall—confirm current App Builder labels.
Publisher layouts in Classic Chatter are a neighboring historical surface.
The analogy does not encode every action type in the wizard.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Quick actions are Lightning and mobile shortcuts. Global actions have no record context and live on the global publisher layout. Object-specific actions belong to an object and can relate creates to this record. You must add the action to a layout or Lightning page or it will not show.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: Create Inspection is object-specific on Property so the lookup prefills. Create Vendor from the header with no record is global. Log a Call on Property is object-specific. I add them to the action bar. I design the action layout fields. I do not replace validation with a button. I mention Dynamic Actions as a Lightning visibility option—Needs verification for the object.

terminology.plain: A shortcut button in Lightning or mobile.
terminology.precise: An action users launch to create or update records, log a call, or open custom UI. Metadata plus placement.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Custom button/link: older related feature, neighboring.

terminology.plain: A shortcut with no current record.
terminology.precise: Not tied to a particular object or record. Assigned via the global publisher layout and other supported global lists.
terminology.example: Create Vendor from the app header.
terminology.non_example: Create Inspection that must parent to this property.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Global publisher layout: the lobby wall.

terminology.plain: A shortcut that belongs to an object.
terminology.precise: Created on an object; can create a related record for the current row; placed on that object's layouts or Lightning page.
terminology.non_example: A global Create Inspection with a blank lookup.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Related list New button: similar idea, different surface.

terminology.precise: The layout that controls which global actions appear in global action areas.
terminology.example: Added LAB_NewVendor to the global publisher layout.
terminology.boundary: Forgetting this is why global actions vanish.

terminology.precise: The field arrangement for that action's create or update screen, not the object's page layout.
terminology.example: Inspection action asks only Date and Type.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Compact layout: highlights, not the action form.
terminology.boundary: FLS still applies to those fields.

terminology.plain: Where record actions show in Lightning.
terminology.precise: The Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions section of the page layout, or actions added on the Lightning record page.
terminology.example: Create Inspection visible on the Property highlight panel actions.
terminology.boundary: Override the default action list when you customize it.

terminology.plain: The new child already points at this record.
terminology.precise: Object-specific create actions can set the relationship to the current record; global creates cannot.
terminology.example: Inspection.Property__c filled from the Property action.
terminology.non_example: User must search Property on a global create.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Default field values: a different feature (DATA-002).
terminology.boundary: This is the usual reason to pick object-specific.

terminology.plain: Actions assigned on the Lightning page with visibility rules.
terminology.precise: A Lightning alternative to the layout action list. Availability is object- and release-sensitive—Needs verification.
terminology.example: Show Create Inspection only when Status is Occupied.
terminology.boundary: Do not promise it on every object.

when_to_use: When users need a Lightning or mobile quick action to create or update a record or log a call.
When the shortcut must know the current record—use an object-specific action so the relationship can prefill.
When the shortcut must work from the header with no record open—use a global action and the global publisher layout.
When you must place an existing action on a page layout or Lightning page so it becomes visible.
When the action form should show a short action layout, not the full page layout.
when_not_to_use: Do not use a global action when the new record must automatically relate to the current record.
Do not use an action as a substitute for a validation rule, formula field, or roll-up.
Do not assume creating the action metadata makes it visible without layout or Lightning placement.
Do not use an action to hide fields from the API (that is FLS) or to replace record types.
Do not build a full custom app as a quick action when a record page or Flow screen is the real need—confirm tool choice.
configuration_or_code_location: Setup → Global Actions, or Object Manager → Buttons, Links, and Actions.
Global publisher layout; object page layout → Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions.
Lightning App Builder → Dynamic Actions if offered.
Action layout editor on the action itself.

interview_questions.question: Compare global and object-specific quick actions.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Global actions are not tied to a record and are placed on the global publisher layout. Object-specific actions belong to an object, can create related records for this row, and are placed on that object's layout or Lightning page.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I pick based on context. Create Vendor from the header is global. Create Inspection from Property is object-specific so the lookup prefills. I always mention placement. I mention validation still runs. I do not invent action-type edition gates.
interview_questions.example: LAB_NewVendor global vs LAB_NewInspection on Property.
tradeoffs: Publisher layout vs record action bar

interview_questions.question: Create Inspection from Property but the Property lookup is blank.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: You probably used a global action. Switch to an object-specific create on Property and include or predefine the relationship field.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open the action definition and check whether it was created on Property. I place it on the Property action bar. I test a LAB_ create. I do not tell users to search the parent every time if the platform can prefill.
interview_questions.example: Replaced a global Create Inspection with an object-specific action; Property__c filled.
tradeoffs: Predefined value vs field on the form
follow_ups: Can a global action accept a record Id parameter?
Should the relationship be hidden on the form?
weak_answer_warnings: Telling users to copy the Id

interview_questions.question: The action is in Setup but missing in Lightning.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: It is not on the page layout action section, the Lightning page, or the global publisher layout. Placement is a second step.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open the layout the user's profile and record type actually use (DATA-008/009). If someone customized the action bar, defaults were replaced and the new action was never added. I do not recreate the action first.
interview_questions.example: Added LAB_NewInspection to Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions; it appeared.
tradeoffs: Dynamic Actions page vs layout list
follow_ups: Which profile's layout are they on?
Did customizing the bar drop standard buttons?

interview_questions.question: When do you refuse a quick action?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the need is a calculated field, a roll-up, a validation gate, or a full screen Flow that is not really a shortcut. Also when a related-list New button already matches the job.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep actions for frequent Lightning/mobile shortcuts. I do not replace DATA-010 with a button that omits a field. I do not build a second object to hold a button. I mention custom LWC/Flow actions as options without inventing compiler details.
interview_questions.example: Rejected an action that existed only to skip Region; wrote a validation rule instead.
tradeoffs: Related list New vs quick action
follow_ups: When is a Flow screen action better?
When is a custom LWC action better?

interview_questions.question: Action layout versus page layout versus compact layout?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Action layout is the create/update form for that action. Page layout is the record's fields, related lists, and action bar. Compact layout is the highlights header.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I can show three fields on Create Inspection and twenty on the Inspection record page. FLS still applies to both. Compact layout will not add the button. Interviewers listen for the three surfaces.
interview_questions.example: Inspection action layout: Date, Type; Inspection page layout: full fields plus related lists.
tradeoffs: Where the button lives vs what the form asks
follow_ups: Does action layout required equal field Required?
Can predefined values set hidden fields?

interview_questions.question: Log a Call from Property and from the header with no record.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Object-specific Log a Call on Property for in-room context. If they also need logging with no record open, that is a different global action—and it will not auto-relate to a property.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I ask whether the Task must link to the property. If yes, object-specific. If they insist on a header button, I warn the lookup will be blank unless they pick a record. I place each action on the matching layout.
interview_questions.example: Property action bar has Log a Call; no global Log a Call unless they accept no prefill.
follow_ups: Is Log a Call a standard action type?
How do Activities relate to Property?
weak_answer_warnings: One global Log a Call for every case

interview_questions.question: Show Create Inspection only when Status is Occupied.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If Dynamic Actions are available on that Lightning page, use a visibility rule. Otherwise use layouts by record type/profile or accept the button is always there and validation/UI handles misuse.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I mark Dynamic Actions object support Needs verification. I do not create OccupiedProperty__c. I do not use FLS to hide an action. I still keep the object-specific action definition.
interview_questions.example: Dynamic Actions visibility Status = Occupied on the Property Lightning page, if offered.

interview_questions.question: How do actions fit with page layouts and Dynamic Forms?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Page layouts still host the Lightning/mobile action list unless Dynamic Actions take over. Dynamic Forms is about fields and sections, not the same as Dynamic Actions. Creating an action does not change the page layout furniture.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: DATA-009 taught four presentation surfaces. This lesson adds the action bar as a fifth placement concern. I assign actions the same way I assign layouts: by the layout the user actually gets. I mention validation still runs from the action save.
interview_questions.example: Commercial Facilities layout includes Create Inspection; Finance layout does not.
follow_ups: Do related-list buttons replace quick actions?
What happens if you override the default action list?
weak_answer_warnings: Saying Dynamic Forms places quick actions
